idiom_name: conditional ASP.NET Core middleware (app.Use / UseWhen branch)
implementation_notes: The request pipeline is the route: add the audit or validation middleware with app.Use only while the configuration flag is set, or branch with UseWhen(predicate, branch => branch.UseMiddleware<AuditMiddleware>()) so the branch is rejoined to the main pipeline and the same endpoint handles the message on both legs. For broker flows (MassTransit) the equivalent stage is a consume filter - IFilter<ConsumeContext> added per endpoint with UseConsumeFilter - which wraps processing exactly like middleware wraps a request. Keep the destination in one terminal endpoint: two handlers, one per leg, is how the two paths drift apart.
pitfalls: The pipeline is assembled once at start-up: a runtime toggle needs a per-request predicate or feature-flag check inside a middleware, not an if around app.Use.
Ordering is part of the contract - a detour registered after the terminal endpoint (Run) never executes, and registering it before the error handler changes error responses while it is on.
Middleware built at start-up must not capture scoped services; resolve per request through InvokeAsync parameters or an explicit scope.
